# Postgres Gotchas

> Known PostgreSQL patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never retrofits constraints onto existing tables](create-table-if-not-exists-stale-constraints.md): Boot-applied schema.sql skips the whole CREATE statement on existing tables, so added FK ON DELETE CASCADE / SET NULL clauses never reach prod; code looks correct while the live constraint stays stale. HIGH.
- [ON CONFLICT must echo an expression-based unique index](on-conflict-expression-index.md): Upserting against a unique index on expressions (e.g. LEAST/GREATEST) requires repeating the exact expression in ON CONFLICT, not bare columns, or it errors 42P10. MEDIUM.
- [ORDER BY ... DESC defaults to NULLS FIRST, inverting a boolean preference clause](order-by-desc-nulls-first.md): A `ORDER BY (nullable_col = $1) DESC LIMIT 1` tie-break silently returns the opposite of its intent, because non-matching NULL rows evaluate to NULL (not false) and DESC sorts NULLS FIRST; add NULLS LAST. HIGH.
- [A column that exists but is NULL corpus-wide makes any filter on it silently match zero rows](filter-on-empty-column-matches-nothing.md): A column can be correctly typed and SELECTed by shipped code yet never written by the crawler/ETL, so `WHERE col <= $1` returns an empty set forever with no error and HTTP 200; profile with `count(col)` vs `count(*)` before building any predicate, and verify a deploy by diffing filtered vs unfiltered DATA rather than by status code. HIGH.
- [An empty cached column can be upstream-null, with the real signal in a sibling field the ETL drops](upstream-null-column-signal-in-dropped-sibling.md): On finding a NULL-corpus-wide column in an API-cached table, "the crawler is behind, re-crawl it" is often wrong -- the upstream may send null permanently while the real value arrives in a sibling field the upsert never gave a column, so the fix is a schema + ETL change rather than an ops rerun; profile the upstream payload and diff the ETL's insert column list against it, and beware that the deadest column is usually the best-named one for your use case. HIGH.
- [Retire the old live owner before transferring a partial-unique key](partial-unique-owner-transfer-order.md): An immediate partial unique index rejects a replacement owner if the old live row is retired later in the same transaction; soft-delete the old owner first. MEDIUM.
- [An empty API result makes a `NOT (col = ANY($1))` delete sweep wipe the whole table](empty-result-any-sweep-deletes-everything.md): The upsert-then-delete-what-was-not-returned reconciliation pattern is correct for every input except the empty array -- `ANY('{}')` matches nothing, so `NOT (...)` is TRUE for every row and the sweep deletes the tenant's entire mirror; an empty list arrives on a successful HTTP 200 from an outage, a revoked/downgraded credential, a renamed response key that a defensive `Array.isArray` guard turns into `[]`, or a pagination bug, and a snapshot job running after the sweep writes the loss into history where it cannot be backfilled. HIGH.
